record_type_quote: The purpose of the proposed study was to conduct a preregistered conceptual replication that investigates the role of intensity in two types of auditory distraction.

targets.title: Auditory encoding in visual short-term recall: Effects of noise intensity and spatial location.
targets.evidence_quote: In all seven experiments conducted so far, the changing-state effect on serial recall was independent of intensity (Colle, 1980; Ellermeier & Hellbrück, 1998; Schlittmeier et al., 2008; Tremblay & Jones, 1999), and this was also the case in the present study.
targets.outcome_quote: We replicated the classic finding that the increased disruption by changing-state relative to steady-state sequences is independent of intensity. Contrary to previous studies, we found an unexpected main effect of intensity. Steady-state and changing-state sequences presented at 75 dB(A) were more disruptive than presented at 45 dB(A), suggesting that intensity plays a more important role than previously assumed in the disruption of working memory performance.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly confirm intensity-independent changing-state disruption but contrast their overall intensity effect with this original’s reported null intensity effect. Both comparisons concern the same target.
